title: Choose the checkout structure
question: Your visual world stays as it is. Choose how the cart, checkout and order page are organised. Steer with a note if something is missing.

options.label: Cart drawer + one-page checkout
options.thesis: Review the cart without leaving the shop; check out on one page with the total always in view.
options.viewport: The navbar bag opens a cream drawer over the page: items with pack, allergens, quantity and price; subtotal and Checkout pinned at the bottom.
options.risk: Drawer plus a separate full cart page is two places to maintain; long carts scroll inside the drawer.

options.label: Step-by-step checkout
options.thesis: One decision per screen, sized for one hand: Cart, You, Delivery, Pay.
options.viewport: A progress row, one big question in Luckiest Guy, three delivery tiles with price and ETA, and the total incl. delivery above Continue.
options.risk: More taps for returning or desktop shoppers; review of the whole order happens late.

options.label: Delivery-first cart
options.thesis: The cart answers 'what will I actually pay?' first: delivery choice and free-delivery progress sit above the items.
options.viewport: A caramel progress meter 'R270 away from free delivery', a Courier / PUDO / Collect switch with prices, then the items, with the total incl. delivery pinned at the bottom.
options.risk: Upsell-adjacent meter must stay honest; checkout still needs a details page after the cart.

options.label: Order pass (fused)
options.lineage: boarding pass and live gate board
options.thesis: The thank-you page as a segmented order pass whose status band changes colour and holds it until you've seen it.
options.viewport: Order, Via and ETA segments over a caramel status band, then the timeline.
options.case: Fuses cleanly into tracking and can sit on top of any of the three checkout structures; loses on scope because it only shapes the order page.
options.risk: Pushed too far it reads as travel, not baking.

options.label: Newsprint circle catalog
options.case: Shoppers don't identify with event catalogs and density hurts a two-item cart.
options.kept: Mark state by hand: the chosen delivery option is visibly 'circled', not just tinted.

options.label: Crouwel grid specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible grid.
options.case: Conflicts with the committed type system.
options.kept: Strict column alignment for prices and totals (tabular figures on one right edge).

options.label: Metro tiles
options.thesis: Flat tiles and cropped giant type.
options.case: Wrong palette and gesture model for a cream bakery checkout.
options.kept: Selection floods the chosen tile instead of adding a small checkmark.

options.label: Zoo guide map
options.case: Organic regions obscure form fields and totals.
options.kept: One dominant region per screen on mobile.

options.label: Variable font specimen
options.kept: Live readouts: totals update in place as choices change.
